leads.title: Planet Shred Records Management LLC v. 2301 Atlantic Avenue LLC (NJ Appellate Division affirms dismissal of tenant's suit against its warehouse/office landlord)
leads.why: New Jersey Appellate Division opinion decided today (Nov 23, 2026) affirms dismissal of a commercial tenant's suit against its Wall Township warehouse/office landlord. Plaintiffs Planet Shred Records Management LLC and Planet Shred LLC (records-storage/shredding business) sued defendants 2301 Atlantic Avenue LLC and JD Commercial & Industrial Properties LLC over a rent dispute, after an earlier landlord-tenant eviction action was resolved by a September 27, 2024 consent judgment (tenant paid $51,032.28, agreed to vacate by March 31, 2025). The panel held the consent judgment operated as an accord and satisfaction barring the tenant's later claims (duress/economic coercion, breach of the implied covenant of good faith and fair dealing, wrongful eviction, NJ Consumer Fraud Act). leads.title: Caruthers v. Sangamon County Board (Illinois circuit court reportedly dismisses challenge to CyrusOne data center conditional-use permit)
leads.why: A law firm client alert (AFSLaw, 'Illinois Voters Push Back on Data Centers as Courts Uphold Local Approvals') states that on November 6, 2026 the Sangamon County, IL circuit court dismissed, applying rational-basis review, a challenge to the Sangamon County Board's April 2026 approval of a conditional-use permit for CyrusOne's roughly $500 million, ~280-acre data center campus near Waverly, IL. The underlying suit -- filed July 6, 2026 by several Waverly-area residents (including the Caruthers family) against Sangamon County and the County Board -- was reported at the time by Illinois Times and the Springfield Business Journal. leads.title: Haleiwa Town Center v. Trustees of the Estate of Bernice Pauahi Bishop (Hawaii Supreme Court reinstates shopping-center tenant's lease claims against Kamehameha Schools)
leads.why: Hawaii Supreme Court opinion decided today (Nov 23, 2026), SCWC-20-0000586, a genuine commercial real estate primary source (full holding is within the stored excerpt even though the opinion runs to 85,788 characters and the stored text is truncated at 12,000). Haleiwa Town Center, LLC (HTC), the long-term ground lessee operating the Haleiwa Town Center shopping center on O'ahu, sued its landlord, the Trustees of the Estate of Bernice Pauahi Bishop aka Kamehameha Schools (KS), over KS's adjacent Hale'iwa Store Lots development: HTC alleged KS misrepresented where a historic access lane (Kewalo Lane) sat relative to HTC's leased premises, tried to push kuleana-owner access obligations onto HTC's property, and encroached onto HTC's leased lot and parking during construction, all breaching the lease's quiet-enjoyment clause. The circuit court had dismissed HTC's complaint and the Intermediate Court of Appeals affirmed; the Supreme Court now holds HTC stated viable breach-of-contract and breach-of-the-implied-covenant-of-good-faith-and-fair-dealing claims (though not its unfair-competition claim), vacates the ICA's award of appellate attorneys' fees to KS since there is no prevailing party yet, and remands to circuit court for further proceedings. Business entities on both sides (HTC and KS); Hawaii has only 2 other tracked matters in js/data.js, so this also helps the site's geographic-diversity gap. Checked js/data.js: not already tracked.
